customer_question: The BLE module we previously registered with has become EOL, so we switched to an alternative module from a different vendor. Our product's name and model number aren't changing -- does this still require a brand-new SIG registration?
question_variants: Do we need to re-register just because we swapped to a replacement BLE module?
Since our product name/model is unchanged, can we skip a new registration?
Does an EOL-driven module substitution count as a new design for SIG purposes?
actual_issue: A previously-registered product's BLE module reached end-of-life and was replaced with an alternative module from a different chip vendor; although the end product's commercial name and model designation remained unchanged, it needed to be confirmed whether this module substitution required an entirely new Bluetooth SIG registration.
plain_english_explanation: Bluetooth certification is tied to the actual radio module and chip design inside a product, not to the product's brand name or model number. If the part that actually handles Bluetooth gets swapped out for a different one -- even as a routine like-for-like replacement when the original part is discontinued -- that's a different design from SIG's point of view and needs its own new registration, even though nothing about the product's name changes for customers.
consultant_answer: Yes, as the customer themselves recognized, a new registration is required. The quote was based on the new module being an antenna-embedded module, and proceeded as a new registration referencing the new module as a Single Design, with agency registration support and compliance folder preparation as separate line items, plus a separate Qualification Fee payable directly to SIG.
decision_logic: Bluetooth SIG registration is tied to the underlying module/Controller design actually used in the product, not to the product's commercial name or model number; substituting the Bluetooth module -- even a routine EOL-driven, like-for-like replacement -- changes the design being certified and therefore requires a new registration, regardless of whether the end product's branding changes.
final_recommendation: Treat any Bluetooth module substitution, including an EOL-driven replacement with no change to the end product's name or model, as requiring a new SIG registration referencing the new module's design.
risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming the existing registration still applies because the end product's name is unchanged would leave the actual shipped product, now using a different Bluetooth module, without valid certification for that hardware.
